title: quorum-based-region-election-and-warm-cache-verification-runbook
creator: Ava Chen
description: Background: We need a deterministic, observable mechanism to pick the target region(s) during global failover windows that avoids split-brain routing and reduces cold-cache penalties. Current warm-standby workflows are manual and rely on ad-hoc priming; this ticket implements a quorum-based region election combined with proactive KV-prefetch verification to ensure standby readiness before traffic cutover. Goals: 1) Define a quorum election protocol that takes region health, capacity headroom, and SLO risk into account. 2) Implement a preflight readiness verification that runs KV-prefetch probes, synthetic inference, and model-variant fallback checks. 3) Expose readiness score and deterministic decision reason in the Console and routing decisions. 4) Provide an automated rollback/circuit-breaker when readiness score degrades during cutover. Scope: - Controller that computes region election using weighted quorum (health, capacity, recent error-rate, latency percentile, model-variant compatibility). - Readiness verifier that runs three checks: (a) KV-prefetch success and hit-rate baseline, (b) synthetic inference with target model variant(s) and latency bound, (c) fallback chain validation (can fallback to quantized variant without >5% quality regress). - Integration with Smart Router to gate traffic shifts until readiness threshold met, with hysteresis and retry windows. - Runbook and automated playbook for on-call to promote/demote standby, with step-by-step checks and dashboard links. Non-goals: full autoscaling policy changes; separate rollout of multi-model batching optimizations (tracked in other tickets).
acceptance_criteria: Controller computes a single winning region with justification string returned in API (health, capacity score, latency p95)
Readiness verifier produces a numeric score 0..100 and stores last 3 probe results
Smart Router refuses >10% incremental traffic shifts to a region with readiness <80
Console shows readiness score and last probe timestamps on region overview page
Automated rollback triggers when readiness score drops >20 points during a cutover and restores previous traffic split within 2 minutes

comments: 2025-11-16 - Ava Chen: Kickoff meeting notes: agreed on weighted quorum approach and that capacity headroom will cap a region's effective score at 80% when lower than target. Action: Mateo to draft scoring function.

2025-11-17 - Mateo Ruiz: Drafted scoring function; pushed prototype controller branch. Key trade-off: counting recentErrorRate reduces flapping but can penalize regions recovering from transient infra events. Proposal: introduce a recovery window and a decay factor.

2025-11-18 - Priya Nair (SRE): Ran chaos test in staging to simulate region egress throttling. Prefetch probes failed 70% of the time until we increased the admission window. Suggest adding an exponential backoff for prefetch retries and a max wall time for verification.

2025-11-19 - Mateo Ruiz: Implemented probe runner with histogram exports and per-model variant probe config. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/778. Early staging runs show p95 within SLO for base model; fallback variant latency is 1.4x slower on avg.

2025-11-20 - Design review (Emilia Park): Console mockups approved pending minor copy changes. Need explicit explanation of 'readiness score' calculation visible to users. Added acceptance criterion to show justification string.

2025-11-21 - Mateo Ruiz: Integrated readiness gating into Smart Router. Deployed to canary (10% of traffic for internal tenants). Observed minor oscillation at the 10% step when a dependent capacity autoscaler kicked in; mitigated by introducing a 'stabilization hold' of 90s between shifts.

2025-11-22 - QA (Omar Singh): Synthetic inference validation completed across three models and two quantized variants. Quality delta <4% for targeted prompts. Starting prep for a full smoke run in preprod with 30-minute ramp.
